name: Wahluke Slope

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay and Syrah sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 2°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
